subject: physics
title: Energy transfers in everyday appliances
key_idea: An appliance transfers more energy the greater its power and the longer it is on. Energy transferred is E = P t. When charge flows, energy transferred is E = Q V, so potential difference is energy per unit charge.

blocks.text: Everyday electrical appliances are designed to bring about energy transfers. This section covers where the energy goes.

items: Appliances transfer energy from batteries or the a.c. mains.
Motors transfer it to kinetic energy.
Heating devices transfer it to thermal energy.
Some energy is wasted as heat in motors and heating devices.
The amount of energy an appliance transfers depends on its power and on how long it is switched on.
A kettle rated at 2100 W transfers 2100 J every second.
A higher power rating means the stored energy changes faster.

blocks.text: Compare appliances using power × time, not power alone. A 100 W television used for 5 hours transfers more energy than a 2000 W toaster used for 0.2 hours.

items: Appliances transfer energy from batteries or the mains to kinetic energy or thermal energy.
Energy transferred depends on the power and the time switched on.
A higher power rating means more energy is transferred each second.

blocks.text: Work is done when charge flows in a circuit. There are two equations for the energy transferred.

blocks.label: Energy from power and time
blocks.formula: energy transferred = power × time    (E = P t)
where: energy transferred, E, in joules, J

blocks.label: Energy from charge and potential difference
blocks.formula: energy transferred = charge flow × potential difference    (E = Q V)
where: energy transferred, E, in joules, J
charge flow, Q, in coulombs, C
potential difference, V, in volts, V

blocks.label: Energy from current, potential difference and time
blocks.formula: energy transferred = current × potential difference × time    (E = I V t)
where: energy transferred, E, in joules, J
potential difference, V, in volts, V

blocks.text: Potential difference as energy per unit charge

items.meaning: The energy transferred per unit charge passed.
The unit of potential difference. One volt is one joule per coulomb.

blocks.text: A potential difference of 6.0 V means 6.0 joules of energy are transferred for every coulomb of charge.

items.text: Change kJ to J and minutes to seconds. 3.6 kJ = 3600 J.
Power and time: E = P t. Charge and potential difference: E = Q V.
To find time, t = E ÷ P. To find charge, Q = E ÷ V.

items: E = P t and E = Q V. Energy is in joules.
Potential difference is energy transferred per unit charge. One volt is one joule per coulomb.
Convert minutes, kJ, kW and mW to seconds, J and W first.

checks.q: A heater has a power of 2000 W. Calculate the energy it transfers in 3 minutes.

What does a potential difference of 6.0 V mean in terms of energy and charge?
checks.a: 6.0 joules of energy are transferred for each coulomb of charge that passes.

worked_example.question: The hair straighteners have a maximum power output of 120 W. The energy transferred to the hair straighteners to reach normal operating temperature is 3.6 kJ. Calculate the time taken for the hair straighteners to reach normal operating temperature when operating at maximum power.
worked_example.tip: One mark each for the conversion to joules, the substitution, the rearrangement and the answer.

worked_example.question: An electric water pump is powered by the 230 V mains supply. The 230 V mains supply transfers 9000 J of energy to the pump motor in 1 minute. Calculate the current in the pump motor. Use the equation I = E / (V × t)
worked_example.tip: One mark each for converting the time, substituting and evaluating.

worked_example.question: A medical freezer is used to keep vaccines cool. The freezer needs 28 500 J of energy to cool the vaccines. It takes 5 minutes for the freezer to cool the vaccines. Calculate the power of the freezer.
worked_example.tip: The time must be in seconds. Using 5 minutes gives 5700 W and loses marks.
